Headway is an estimate, not sourced: about four trains each way a day, from the 1916 e-WV count.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 68.3 mi against 68.7 mi documented (1922 ETT Corning - Point Pleasant; Fowler route 17 57.2 - 125.9). Made of: Corning - Hobson 56.0 mi (Fowler 56.2, ICC 56.8 owned) on NYC-tagged ways (55.3 mi) + 0.8 mi untagged rail; Hobson - Kanauga junction 10.2 mi (Fowler 10.2); Kanauga junction - Point Pleasant 2.1 mi over the Ohio River bridge on NYC-tagged track (Fowler 2.3, ETT 2.6). No straight-line legs; every station waypoint within 0.8 km except Rutland village (1.3 km, the station lay outside the village). HOBSON - KANAUGA (c.10 mi) is Hocking Valley (later C&O Pomeroy Subdivision) track that K&M/NYC trains used under an operating arrangement (Fowler: 'operated over CO'); traced on C&O-tagged ways (live and abandoned), 9.2 mi C&O-tagged + 0.7 mi untagged rail. HOBSON - RUTLAND: drawn on the original line via Rockville and the west side of Middleport (NYC-tagged railway=abandoned), forced with via points, because Fowler's mileposts run Hobson 69.7 - Middleport 71.2 - Rockville 71.8 - Rutland 74.7. The live Kanawha River Railroad cut-off between Rutland and Hobson is a later, undated alignment and is not drawn. ATHENS: the drawn line bypasses Athens on the Chauncey - Armitage - Grosvenor alignment (live NYC-tagged track; OpenHistoricalMap way -198202886 dates it to the Ohio Central, 1880 - not independently checked). Passenger trains did not run that way throughout: Fowler notes 1900G timings imply service originally went over the B&O between Grosvenor and Athens, and by 1905 (Athens Union Station marked 'reverse') trains ran into Athens from Armitage and backed out. Neither movement is drawn on this feature (the 1905-1909 Armitage - Athens stub is its own feature). Fowler's mileages include the Athens movement, which is part of why documented route mileage runs about 1-2 mi above the drawn length. KANAUGA: the drawn connection from the Hocking Valley at Kanauga junction round a loop onto the Ohio River bridge is the present (NYC-tagged) track; the ICC lists a 1.22-mi K&M 'Kanauga to the Hocking Valley Railway' connection built 1911, so for years before 1911 the last c.1 mi on the Ohio bank may be a later alignment than the era's (the earlier arrangement was not found).

segments.note: K&M Ohio Division, Corning (junction with the T&OC, over which through trains ran on to Columbus and Toledo) - Glouster - Athens - Rutland - Hobson, then over the Hocking Valley via Cheshire and Addison to Kanauga and across the Ohio River bridge to Point Pleasant. Starts 1893: Fowler z (1893G) at Corning and Hatfield is the first confirmed K&M-era year (only the ambiguous 1890G Newton listing touches 1890-1892). Fowler a (1905G) at nearly every station Kanauga - Glouster and w (1915w) at Rockville, Meigs, Grosvenor, Doty, College Hill. Ends 31 Dec 1921 as an operator era (1 Jan 1922 lease to T&OC/NYC); continues as nyc-kanawha-michigan-corning-point-pleasant. Through trains Athens: see geometry_quality. Headway is an estimate, not sourced: about four through trains each way a day, as on the WV side.
